summary: An Owner can move an active physical group one place from the selected browser board's heading menu. The preview-only group-order POST calls store::reorder_groups, which checks the board revision and exact active membership under the board lock. Dense positions, every included group's revision and the board revision commit together. Reload board reads the accepted order before another menu choice.
evidence: All 40 browser_preview journeys passed in owned headless Chromium. browser_moves_group_one_place_from_menu checked the first, last and sole group controls, dismissal, duplicate Work headings and an empty neighbour. Holding the board lock kept the original grid visible with exactly one POST. At board/8 the order was g-z [61,63], g-old [59], g-end []; positions were 0,1,2 and all three revisions were 2. Down and document reload preserved IDs, counts and child order.

browser_reloads_order_before_moving_group_again checked a deferred 500 against the intact /8 snapshot before removing the fault. A new Down committed /9. After the peer committed [g-old,g-end,g-z] at /10, the stale Up received 409. Reload sent only GET. A new Up moved past g-end at /10, committing /11 and group revisions 5. The following GET returned 503; a read-only retry displayed the committed order. Each write's path, complete ID array and baseline were checked independently of grouped and flat readbacks and fresh board/group/item/receipt snapshots.

browser_demoted_owner_cannot_reorder_groups observed one 403 after the enabled menu was opened, then an authorized reread. Both move choices were disabled for Member and Viewer; only Member retained item editing. Withdrawing workspace membership hid the grid; revoking the session returned to sign-in. Structural snapshots were unchanged.

All 31 loopback_board_access tests passed. The two packet cases covered session, role (including Member creator), workspace and board grants/states, route isolation, same board-local ID on another board, malformed requests, revision checks, bounded membership and incomplete/invalid permutations. A current same-order request advanced all revisions. Two competing valid orders yielded one 200 and one 409; stale replay conflicted. A deferred refusal rolled back ranks and revisions, with inactive, archived and foreign rows and receipts unchanged.

cargo fmt --all -- --check and git diff --check passed. cargo test --locked --workspace passed all 46 tests using target-browser-packets and the disposable database. An initial focused host build could not link its test executable (LNK1104); both complete host-suite runs subsequently passed. Worker shell policy denied node --test scripts/run.test.mjs before execution. Lost POST acknowledgments and late responses after navigation were not separately fault-injected.
